issues.detail: Error handling is thin: the examples don't check upstream fetch status (a failed origin response is cached in KV for 5 minutes), and the scheduled sync has no handling for failed fetches or D1 batch errors.

scenarios.name: kv-cached-api-worker
scenarios.rationale: B scaffolds with `npm create cloudflare@latest`, creates the KV namespace, uses a pinned compatibility_date, reads KV first, uses `expirationTtl` 600 and `Env`, and gives `wrangler dev` and `wrangler deploy`, while A omits `npm create cloudflare@latest` and scaffolds by hand with `npm init`, though it covers the other points.

scenarios.name: cron-sync-into-d1
scenarios.rationale: Both cover d1 create, migrations create/apply, d1_databases, the */30 cron under triggers.crons, and a scheduled handler using prepare with batch; A also uses ctx.waitUntil (which the rubric allows), adds pagination, a watermark and retries, while B is simpler, handles only a single response page, and does not use waitUntil.

scenarios.name: secrets-and-local-dev-pitfalls
scenarios.rationale: Both cover `wrangler types`, `wrangler tail`, and why `wrangler dev` doesn't see production KV (local simulation, `--remote`); A explicitly says not to put the key in wrangler.jsonc and notes secrets are per-environment, while B only warns against `vars` in wrangler.toml and never says secrets are per-environment, but B is far more thorough on the other parts, including the `.dev.vars` handling, the tail options, and seeding local KV.
